notes: Every name invented by the narrative stream, with the WORLD_BIBLE §5 rule it follows. Data, not prose: kept in the pack so a later pass can diff new names against it and so tools/namegen.py --check has a roster to compare. 'derivation' cites the roots and suffixes in §5.1-5.4.

rows.name: Wren Tallow
rows.derivation: bible example, §5.1

rows.name: Osric Pennywort
rows.derivation: bible example, §5.1

rows.name: Winnow Pennywort
rows.derivation: winnow (a mill word), family surname Pennywort = penny 'small'

rows.name: Hallam Ashdown
rows.derivation: hal- + -am; surname ash + -down, bible example

rows.name: Maud Brambling
rows.derivation: bible example, §5.1

rows.name: Tobin Cresswell
rows.derivation: Tobin (§5.1 first names); surname cress + -well

rows.name: Nell Harebell
rows.rule: 5.1 people; surname from two Valish roots
rows.derivation: hare + bell

rows.name: Corwen Mullard
rows.derivation: cor- + -en; surname Mullard from mull 'soft soil'

rows.name: Bessa Tamwick
rows.derivation: surname is the hamlet Tamwick (tam 'oak' + -wick)

rows.name: Robin Ashdown
rows.derivation: bird-name first name; father's surname

rows.name: Ellard Wynstead
rows.derivation: surname wyn 'meadow' + -stead

rows.name: Merrick Gosling
rows.derivation: merrow 'calm water' shortened + -ick; surname gos 'goose' + -ling

rows.name: Hesta Hollins
rows.derivation: surname from hollin 'holly'

rows.name: Pellam Ashcombe
rows.derivation: pell- + -am; surname ash + -combe

rows.name: Tam Hollins
rows.derivation: tam 'oak'; Hesta's late husband, named in dialogue only

rows.name: Aldith Sulion
rows.derivation: surname sul 'light' + -ion, an Oroth ending on a Tollmere family

rows.name: Bennick Cresswell
rows.derivation: Merrowby-born; cousin to Tobin Cresswell

rows.name: Ismay Ondrael
rows.derivation: ondr 'deep' + -ael; taken from a ruin by her mother's people, as the book says

rows.name: Tamsin Wick
rows.rule: 5.1 people; surname from a place suffix
rows.derivation: -wick 'dwelling' used bare as a surname

rows.name: Orrin Quill
rows.derivation: Quill, a clerk's trade name

rows.name: Aud Fennick
rows.rule: 5.1 people: masculine/neutral -ick used for a woman, per 'many names are used for anyone'
rows.derivation: surname from fenn

rows.name: Alder Wyke
rows.rule: 3.5 Woodfolk: Valish dialect with old roots
rows.derivation: alder (tree); Wyke, an older spelling of -wick

rows.name: Cadwen Ash
rows.rule: 5.1 people: -en; second name is a taken order-name, not a family name
rows.derivation: cad 'hill' + -en; 'Ash' sworn at Pilgrim's Ash

rows.name: Half-Ell
rows.rule: deliberate breach: the Quiet Hands do not use names (4, 5.1)
rows.derivation: a cloth measure; a by-name standing where a name was given up

rows.name: Tallissa Oul
rows.rule: 5.4: soft, sibilant, vowel-final, doubled consonants for length
rows.derivation: tal 'patience' + -lissa (cf. lissa 'reed'); Oul 'deep pool'

rows.name: Sa'oul
rows.rule: 5.4: the glottal apostrophe appears only in names of the drowned
rows.derivation: bible example; named in the Isseva round

rows.name: Tessane
rows.derivation: the Sayer of the Tide whom the Circle unsaid in Y.T. 941; a Sedgish name in a Tollmere institution, which is the point of her

rows.name: Dunna ko-Kharrow
rows.rule: 5.3: ko- 'child of' before the clan name; short, stress first
rows.derivation: dun 'remembered' + -na; Clan Kharrow

rows.name: Brann ko-Kharrow
rows.derivation: bible example first name, Kharrow clan; sung in the Rope-Song

rows.name: Ushka ko-Kharrow
rows.derivation: bible example first name; a former memory-keeper

rows.name: Orrik ko-Kharrow
rows.derivation: orr 'bone' + -ik; went into the Oskeld shaft after his sister

rows.name: Ghorr
rows.rule: 5.3: clusters gh, rr; clan names are short
rows.derivation: gh- + orr 'bone': the Bone Clan, the eighth verse missing from the Rope-Song

rows.name: Mullbourne
rows.derivation: mull 'soft soil' + -bourne 'stream' — the soft ground of the quiet hamlet

rows.name: Harewell
rows.derivation: hare + -well: the well with a hare cut on its lip

rows.name: Larkstead
rows.derivation: lark + -stead; a quiet hamlet on the Roll

rows.name: Gosford
rows.derivation: gos 'goose' + -ford; the hamlet that stopped sending a cart in Y.T. 981

rows.name: Cille
rows.derivation: the Harewell hedge-honey seller nobody can picture

rows.name: Annet
rows.derivation: the writer of the Greyfold letter

rows.name: Ellen
rows.derivation: her sister at Gullhithe

rows.name: Mother Oss
rows.rule: 5.1 people: short form with an honorific
rows.derivation: Greyfold; whose idea the laid tables were

rows.name: Hob Larkin
rows.derivation: Hob (§5.1 first names); lark + -in. The unreliable hunter

rows.name: Tansy Cresswell
rows.derivation: from the POI registry (Foxglove Dell); made Nell Harebell's cousin by this stream

rows.name: Nauve Mor
rows.derivation: bible example; the salt-trader who wrote the Salt Isles guide

rows.name: Brannock
rows.derivation: a dead pilgrim at Pilgrim's Ash, named once by Aud Fennick

rows.name: M. Tarrow
rows.derivation: the Merrowby carter fined four marks in the Lantern Row day-book

rows.name: J. Wick
rows.derivation: the Gullhithe fisher fined forty marks for the same offence; kin to Tamsin Wick

rows.name: Greatsnail
rows.derivation: Winnow Pennywort's league leader; 'Second Greatsnail' is a post, not a snail

rows.name: Fast Colin
rows.derivation: a snail that is not fast; that is the joke

rows.name: Bramble
rows.derivation: Robin Ashdown's dog

rows.name: The Grafted Tree
rows.derivation: Bessa Tamwick's tree carrying eleven dead varieties

rows.name: The Toll's Lip
rows.rule: named for the feature it is built into
rows.derivation: the Merrowby inn whose cellar is the inside of the bell
